subject: Emergency hotpatch: change chronology + SDLC evidence bundle
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@secureassess.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: secops@fintrust.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence for emergency hotpatch on 2027-05-12

Vanessa,

During our SIG review of FinTrust integrations we flagged an emergency hotpatch that was deployed on 2027-05-12 (change id CHG-20270512). To complete the control narrative for Secure SDLC and the incident exemption, please provide the following artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2027-06-01):

- PR(s) and code review threads that cover the hotpatch commit(s) (or an explanation if a bypass occurred)
- CI/CD run logs for the build that promoted the hotpatch (timestamps and job IDs)
- Change control approval records and the justification for the emergency exemption
- Rollback plan used and evidence it was staged/tested
- Any post-deploy verification/runbook steps and owner sign-offs

If some items cannot be exported (sensitive tokens/x), provide redacted logs and a short attestation.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Senior Assessor – SecureAssess

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@secureassess.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for emergency hotpatch on 2027-05-12

Hi Samira — attaching the evidence bundle for CHG-20270512 and a short summary below. Full artifacts are in the Drive link and HubSpot ticket HS-908172. Let me know if you need any additional exports.

Summary (what we included):
- PR list and reviewer comments: 20270512-hotpatch-prs.csv (contains PR IDs, author, reviewers, timestamps). Note: one PR (PR#4512) was merged under an "emergency expedite" flag after a on-call approval; reviewer comments are preserved.
- CI trace: ci-run-20270512.log (build id: build-20270512-77, pipeline: deploy-hotpatch). We redacted ephemeral token values.
- Change approval record: change-approval-record-CHG-20270512.pdf (DocuSign envelope DOC-CHG-20270512, signed by on-call SRE and Product Ops manager).
- Rollback plan: rollback-plan-20270512.txt (steps + tested dry-run results in staging).
- Post-deploy verification: inline notes in the change PDF and gates in the CI log; owners: @marissa_cole (eng mgr) and @karthik_iyer (infra).

Why emergency exception: A zero-day parsing regression was causing memory growth on a live critical queue; mitigation required a one-line input sanitization fix. The fix was low-risk but required immediate rollout due to customer impact. We used the documented emergency workflow (section 4.2 in our change policy) with time-boxed approvals and immediate verification.

Files attached and Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bHotpatchEvidence
HubSpot: HS-908172 (timeline + playbook link)

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- 20270512-hotpatch-prs.csv (csv)
- ci-run-20270512.log (text)
- change-approval-record-CHG-20270512.pdf (pdf)
- rollback-plan-20270512.txt (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for emergency hotpatch on 2027-05-12

Vanessa / Samira — quick clarifications from Engineering: 

- The expedite flag on PR#4512 is visible in the CSV (column: expedite=true). Approver chain: on-call SRE (Karthik) -> Product Ops (A. Huang) via DocuSign.
- CI did run the full test-suite except for nightly integration smoke (we documented the risk). See ci-run-20270512.log lines 1123-1186 for test subset output.
- Secrets handling: the hotpatch pipeline used ephemeral build agent tokens; those tokens are rotated automatically and we have no long-lived secrets in the job. We redacted token string values from the log but preserved job ids.
- Rollback was prepared and dry-run executed in staging at 2027-05-12T03:20:00Z. Results: successful; time to rollback estimated 9 minutes.

If the assessor needs a cross-check, we can export job metadata from our CI (we may need a signed compliance NDA for raw job env vars).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Runtime

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we close the control: 

1) For SIG/CAIQ traceability we need either the full reviewer account IDs for PR#4512 (audit pseudonymization is acceptable) or a short attestation that an automated merge policy was bypassed and why the designated reviewer(s) are the authors of the approval.

2) We also need a signed attestation that the rollback plan was tested with the same DB schema version that was live at time-of-deploy (the staging dry-run note above is good but we need the schema confirmation).

If you can send brief items for these two points (email attestation or short PDF) we'll tag the control as satisfied.

Samira
Senior Assessor – SecureAssess
